dedupe_keys.name: television resilience and national security the case for uk terrestrial broadcast infrastructure arqiva august 2026

description: This Arqiva article, first published by the National Preparedness Commission in June 2026, argues that the UK Government's Media Green Paper gives too little weight to the resilience role of terrestrial broadcast infrastructure. The Green Paper sets out two futures: extending terrestrial TV into the mid-2040s or switching it off by 2034. The author points to a changing risk environment (the invasion of Ukraine, GNSS jamming and spoofing in Europe, cyber attacks on UK businesses), shared-infrastructure failures such as the 2025 Iberian blackout and the Heathrow substation fire, and a UK government estimate that 24 hours of GNSS disruption could cost 1.4 billion pounds. It states that the terrestrial network reaches about 98.5% of households through around 1,400 sites, carries DAB and FM radio and services for over 300 emergency and public-sector organisations, and often has backup power. Producer: Arqiva, a broadcast infrastructure operator with a commercial interest in the outcome. Coverage: United Kingdom. Access: free article; the original NPC page returned an access block to the cloud session. Licence and cost: free to read; licence not stated. Caveats: it is an advocacy piece by an interested operator, with figures cited without their sources. Simulation uses: the reach, site count and dependent-service figures give inputs for national resilience and emergency-communication scenarios. Related record: the Iberian blackout and IXP case study (case_study-iberian-blackout-2025-internet-exchange-points-traffic-bgp-data-centre).
